questions.q: The term **public service** in a democratic administration is best defined as the...
options: body of career officials employed by the government to formulate and implement public policies.
elected political leaders serving temporarily in the national legislature and executive.
private organizations and non-governmental bodies that render voluntary community services.
paramilitary security agencies strictly established to protect the nation's international borders.
questions.explain: In civic education, the **public service** (often embodied by the civil service and public corporations) refers to the permanent, non-partisan body of career administrative officials employed by the government to execute its laws and implement public policies.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 2: Social Vices, National Development & Governance
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: Which of the following represents a primary function of the public service?
options: Sponsoring and campaigning for candidates during general elections
Advising the political executive and faithfully executing government policies
Adjudicating constitutional disputes between the federal and state governments
Passing legislative bills into law and ratifying international treaties
questions.explain: While the legislature makes the law and the judiciary interprets it, the core mandate of the public service is to **implement and execute government policies**. Furthermore, top civil servants use their wealth of experience to **advise political leaders** (like Ministers and Commissioners) on policy formulation.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 2: Social Vices, National Development & Governance
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: During a change of government following a general election, the public service ensures administrative stability primarily because civil servants...
options: are automatically promoted to occupy the vacant executive positions left by politicians.
enjoy permanent career tenure and do not leave office alongside the defeated political leaders.
hold an absolute constitutional veto power over incoming administrative decisions.
possess the legal mandate to suspend the incoming political parties indefinitely.
questions.explain: A major attribute of the public service is **permanence (continuity)**. Unlike elected politicians whose tenure is temporary and changes with elections, civil servants enjoy secure career appointments until retirement, ensuring the continuous survival and administration of the state.

questions.q: A major problem that slows down government operations and leads to chronic inefficiency in the public service is strict, rigid adherence to excessive administrative routines, a phenomenon commonly referred to as...
options: nepotism.
gerrymandering.
red-tapism.
federalism.
questions.explain: **Red-tapism** (or excessive bureaucracy) is the rigid, mechanical observance of official rules, forms, and procedures. This over-reliance on paperwork causes unnecessary delays, frustrating the timely delivery of public services to citizens.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 2: Social Vices, National Development & Governance
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: The efficiency of the public service in Nigeria is frequently undermined when appointments, postings, and promotions are based on tribal affiliations rather than merit. This severe shortcoming is known as...
options: patriotism.
nepotism.
pluralism.
nationalism.
questions.explain: **Nepotism**, tribalism, and favouritism occur when public officials use their authority to recruit or promote their relatives, friends, or tribesmen, completely ignoring professional qualifications and merit. This severely degrades the competence of the workforce.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 2: Social Vices, National Development & Governance
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: Which of the following serves as a prominent reason for the poor attitude to work, low morale, and widespread bribery often witnessed among junior workers in the public service?
options: Regular and advanced international training opportunities for all staff members
Overbearing political interference and extremely poor remuneration
The complete absence of civil or criminal laws within the nation
The mandatory participation of civil servants in violent street protests
questions.explain: Poor conditions of service, delayed payment of pensions, and low salaries (**poor remuneration**) heavily dampen morale. This financial desperation, combined with unchecked political interference, often drives public servants toward bribery and corrupt practices to sustain themselves.
questions.exam: NECO Civic Education Part 2: Social Vices, National Development & Governance
questions.subject: Civic Education

questions.q: In order to drastically improve efficiency, customer satisfaction, and timely service delivery in the Nigerian public service, the federal government initiated a major reform program commonly known as...
options: SERVICOM.
NAFDAC.
NAPTIP.
INEC.
questions.explain: **SERVICOM** (Service Compact with All Nigerians) was established in 2004 as an institutional mechanism by the Federal Government to promote effective and efficient service delivery, thereby holding Ministries, Departments, and Agencies (MDAs) accountable for the quality of services they provide to the public.
